values.higher_rated_conductors: permitted to be used for ampacity adjustment, correction, or both

quote_segments: (C) Temperature Limitations.
The temperature rating associated with the ampacity of a conductor shall be selected and coordinated
so as not to exceed the lowest temperature rating of any connected termination, conductor, or device.
Conductors with temperature ratings higher than specified for terminations shall be permitted
to be used for ampacity adjustment, correction, or both.

determining equipment termination provisions shall be based on Table 310.16 as appropriately

quote_segments: (a) Termination provisions of equipment for circuits rated 100 amperes or less, or marked
for 14 AWG through 1 AWG conductors, shall be used only for one of the following:
(1) Conductors rated 60°C (140°F).
(2) Conductors with higher temperature ratings, provided the ampacity of such conductors is
determined based on the 60°C (140°F) ampacity of the conductor size used.
(3) Conductors with higher temperature ratings if the equipment is listed and identified for use
with such conductors.
(4) For motors marked with design letters B, C, or D, conductors having an insulation rating of
75°C (167°F) or higher shall be permitted to be used, provided the ampacity of such
conductors does not exceed the 75°C (167°F) ampacity.

engine_rules.rule: The ampacity column used may not exceed the lowest temperature rating of any connected termination (both ends), the conductor, or any device.
Circuits rated 100 A or less, or terminals marked for 14–1 AWG: 60 °C column by default.
Circuits rated over 100 A, or terminals marked for conductors larger than 1 AWG: 75 °C column by default.
The 75 °C column for a circuit of 100 A or less only when the reader confirms that the equipment at every termination is listed and identified for use with 75 °C conductors. Never a silent default.
Never offer the 90 °C column as the final ampacity: it needs equipment listed and identified for 90 °C conductors at every termination.
Motors marked design B, C or D: conductors insulated 75 °C or higher may be used at the 75 °C ampacity, even at 100 A or less.

A higher-rated conductor (for example 90 °C) may start from its own column for correction and adjustment; the final ampacity may not exceed the termination column's ampacity for that size. Individual conductors only (not NM or UF cable).
Termination ampacities come from Table 310.16, as modified by 310.12, unless the equipment is listed and marked otherwise.
Separately installed pressure connectors are limited to their own listed and identified temperature rating.

Wiring method NM or UF: 60 °C only, whatever the terminations, until 334.80 and 340.80 are verified. Cite 110.14(C)(1)(a) for circuits of 100 A or less; never cite 334.80. For cable, correction and adjustment start from the 60 °C column; derating-start applies to individual conductors only.

notes: Render values and rules, not long quotes. Do not quote the Informational Note: its wording is a flattened redline in the source; its content (equipment markings or listing may further restrict conductor size and temperature) may be stated in plain words.
(C)(1)(b)(1) and (b)(2) are printed without a final period in SR-7793; the printed edition's punctuation is not verified.
Single-pull pieces: the headings, the (C)(1) first sentence and the (a)(1) wording. Every rule value is confirmed by both pulls.
